title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`), its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model, priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100k. It is about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average and is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting. The release also halves the Sonnet 5.5 cache-read price and adds monthly API credits for Max and Team subscribers, and it suits support, browser use, and subagents, while Sonnet and Opus 5.5 remain better for complex agentic coding.

title: Building effective agent automations
summary: A guide and reference implementation shows how to build scheduled agents on Claude Managed Agents (beta), using a daily Slack and GitHub brief example that is deployed with `ant apply`. It covers six parts (sources, destination, agent config, schedule, memory stores, and guardrails) and reliability patterns such as per-source bookmarks, re-checking live status, and recording a send only after Slack confirms it, along with credential vaults and a per-run budget cap of 3-5x normal cost. These patterns matter because scheduled agents tend to fail quietly, and they target those silent failure modes.

title: How Block orchestrates Claude Fable across thousands of pull requests
summary: Block's Bradley Axen describes using Claude Fable 5 to orchestrate company-wide code migrations that span hundreds to thousands of PRs, with one migration merging a thousand Fable-orchestrated PRs. Fable handles high-level design such as data models and API specs and directs cheaper Opus or Sonnet models to edit files and run tests, which reportedly keeps quality intact while frontier tokens go to planning. Humans still approve merges and production deploys through dual approval, and the model refuses to bypass that step.

title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
summary: Anthropic expanded the Cyber Verification Program, giving vetted security professionals access to top models with fewer cyber safeguards. The program merges Project Glasswing and the prior CVP into three tiers (Defense, Red Team, and Specialized), each including Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1, and data retention is required for misuse monitoring until Enterprise Frontier Safeguards launches this fall. Glasswing partners reportedly found more than 129,000 verified vulnerabilities between April and July 2026.

title: Automating eval design and hillclimbing with Claude
summary: A new playbook adds the `/claude-api build-eval` and `/claude-api hillclimb` commands to the claude-api skill for automating eval design. build-eval interviews you, samples inputs, and waits for approval before choosing a grader and baseline, while hillclimb splits train and test sets and keeps a patch only if both improve, which limits overfitting. In the support benchmark, cost per ticket fell about 80% (4.6c to 1c) and held-out accuracy rose from 78.6% to 90.5%, and the claude-api skill's eval pass rate rose from 66.1% to 87.9%.

title: Claude now works with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides
summary: The Claude for Google Workspace add-on is in public beta on all paid plans, adding a Claude sidebar to Docs, Sheets, and Slides. Claude reads the open file and selection and edits directly, such as restyling, adding formulas or charts, or changing slides, in either 'Ask before edits' or 'Accept all edits' mode. New Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors (beta) let Claude create and edit Google files while respecting sharing permissions, with connectors, skills, and enterprise controls kept inside the add-on.
